newsitem.title: USA: Williams reorganizes to form energy group.
newsitem.headline: Williams reorganizes to form energy group.

text.p: Tulsa, Okla.-based Williams Cos. Inc. said Monday it was reorganizing its unregulated energy businesses to more aggressively compete for a larger share of a rapidly evolving energy market.

Williams, which operates interstate natural gas pipelines as well as a large telecommunications systems, said it will form a new, full-service energy company called Williams Energy Group, effective Oct. 1.

The new structure will combine Williams Field Services Group, Williams Pipe Line Co., Williams Energy Ventures and Williams Energy Services Co. Parts of these businesses will be excluded for regulatory and financial reasons.
Williams' interstate natural gas pipeline, which is regulated, is also not part of the new structure.

"We're meeting the market demand for a full-service energy provider head on by bringing together some of the premier financial players and asset-based players in the energy market," said Keith Bailey, chairman of Williams.

Williams Field Services has the nation's largest natural gas gathering system and one of its largest processing operations. The unit is also involved in gas production and power cogeneration activities.
Williams Pipe Line Co. provides petroleum liquids pipeline transportation and terminal services.
Williams Energy Ventures includes the nation's second largest ethanol producer and is involved in other energy liquid ventures.
Williams Energy Services Co. provides physical and financial services for all energy comodities.

Last week, Williams said its Houston-based WilTel unit, the fifth largest long-distance carrier in the country, acquired SoftIRON Systems Inc., a network systems intergrator based in California, for an undisclosed price.
